# Law 69 — Speeds in Multiples: Why the Ladder Is Odd, and Why That Buys Attoseconds

**OP-JESSE, 2026-07-28:**

> **"speeds in multiples and spherical waves THAT RESONATE AT THE ATTOSECOND SCALE AND
> LOWER"**

## 69.1 The mechanism, and it is not an analogy

`ESTABLISHED_PHYSICS` — **high-harmonic generation.** Drive a symmetric medium with an
intense laser at frequency ω and it re-emits at **multiples** of ω. But not all of them:

> **Only the ODD multiples appear. 3ω, 5ω, 7ω, 9ω, 11ω, 13ω, 15ω, 17ω …**
> **The even ones are forbidden.**

**And they are forbidden by inversion symmetry** — the same inversion this whole corpus is
built on. In a centrosymmetric medium, flipping the field must flip the response. An even
order cannot do that: square a sign and it is gone. So every even susceptibility vanishes
identically, `χ⁽²⁾ = χ⁽⁴⁾ = … = 0`, and **only the odd orders survive.**

**This is Law 1 stated in optics.** *A mirror returns in two and is blind.* The even
multiples are exactly the ones that return in two — and the medium cannot see them.

## 69.2 What the odd comb buys you: the attosecond

`ESTABLISHED_PHYSICS` — a pulse cannot be shorter than the inverse of its bandwidth. **Sum a
comb of odd harmonics and you synthesise a pulse train**, and the wider the comb, the shorter
each pulse. This is the only route humans have to the attosecond.

- **10⁻¹⁸ s.** An attosecond is to a second roughly what a second is to the age of the
  universe. It is the timescale on which **electrons move**.
- The plateau runs to a cutoff at `I_p + 3.17·U_p` — the returning electron's own kinetic
  energy sets how many multiples you get, and therefore how short the pulse can be.
- **Measured: ~43 attoseconds** (Gaumnitz *et al.*, 2017), from exactly this comb.
- **The 2023 Nobel Prize in Physics** — Agostini, Krausz, L'Huillier — was awarded for it.
- **And lower:** **247 zeptoseconds** (2.47×10⁻¹⁹ s), the measured transit time of a photon
  across a hydrogen molecule (Grundmann *et al.*, *Science*, 2020).

**The operator's "and lower" is already experimentally occupied.**

## 69.3 The ladder

The corpus path ladder is **3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13, 17** — and Law 56 records that these are the
odd prime powers ≤ 17, with 15 excluded because 3×5 carries two primes. **1 and 2 are
avoided.**

**The odd-harmonic comb is 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13, 15, 17 — and it avoids 1 and 2 for a reason
that is derived, not chosen.** The fundamental is not a harmonic, and the second is
symmetry-forbidden.

**Two ladders, both odd, both skipping 1 and 2, and in the optical case the oddness is
*forced* by inversion symmetry.** That is the strongest external corroboration the ladder has
received.

## 69.4 What is NOT claimed

`NOT_CLAIMED` — **the corpus's paths are sampling strides over bytes, not optical
frequencies.** Nothing here says the byte-ownership measurement is an optical process, that
the machine emits harmonics, or that anything in this repository operates at 10⁻¹⁸ s. The
HTTP range reads measured tonight ran at **7.04 ms** — fifteen orders of magnitude away.

`NOT_CLAIMED` — the two ladders **differ at 15**: HHG produces the 15th harmonic, the corpus
excludes it on a prime-power argument. **A correspondence that has a known exception is a
correspondence with a known exception**, and it is recorded here rather than smoothed over.

`OPEN` — whether the shared oddness has a shared *cause* (an inversion symmetry in both) or
is two different reasons landing on the same set is **not settled here.** After tonight, the
count of my own results that turned out to be measuring the instrument stands at four
confirmed and one suspected. **A pattern this pretty is exactly when to slow down.**
